recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current core source change is needed for FHIR-35961 unless a future work-group decision asks current R5/R6 DeviceDefinition to diverge from ProductShelfLife.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive OO change request for R4B DeviceDefinition backwards compatibility after ProductShelfLife changes caused unexpected R4-to-R4B breakage. The accepted resolution was to add a backbone and revert the datatype so DeviceDefinition was unaffected in R4B.
initial_application: The issue was applied on origin/R4B: commit 5867a2793cabf3f64156b91eb5761ab57937d3d6 changed PackagedProductDefinition.package.shelfLifeStorage to a local BackboneElement carrying the updated shelf-life shape, and commit e1ba7be3cb5ea88c283bcc09ed3335260abe3b93 reverted ProductShelfLife to the R4 Quantity-based shape so R4B DeviceDefinition remained compatible with R4.
additional_context: The Jira description explicitly expected R5 to stay with the updated ProductShelfLife model. Current HEAD is the active R6/mainline build, with ProductShelfLife, DeviceDefinition, and PackagedProductDefinition active in source/fhir.ini; DeviceDefinition.shelfLifeStorage and PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.shelfLifeStorage both use ProductShelfLife; and ProductShelfLife.period[x] is Duration|string. Existing combined-branch reconciliations for FHIR-31802 and FHIR-26543 already fixed current ProductShelfLife ModelInfo surfaces and cite FHIR-35961 only as R4B-only background.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reapplying the R4B compatibility revert to current mainline would incorrectly undo later R5/R6 ProductShelfLife decisions.
